help.title: Email Studio — How to Use
help.overview.title: What is the Email Studio?
help.overview.text: The Email Studio is the central template builder for all emails in the ABpE Portal. All apps (cv_extractor, ingest_email, matching) send emails exclusively through this central API.
help.overview.modes.title: Sender Modes
help.overview.user.title: USER — Personal
help.overview.user.text: From address = logged-in user. Each employee sends with their own email and signature. Angelo sends as angelo@abcona.de, Tanja as tg@abcona.de.
help.overview.template.title: TEMPLATE — Fixed
help.overview.template.text: From address = fixed configured address (e.g. info@abcona.de). Signature stored on the template. For newsletters, general info mails.
help.overview.auto.title: AUTO — Automated
help.overview.auto.text: From = noreply@abcona.de. No signature. X-Auto-Response-Suppress header set. For system mails (upload confirmation, pipeline status).
help.overview.api.title: Central API
help.overview.api.text: Other apps never send directly via SMTP — always via EmailStudio.send():
help.modules.title: Modules — Reusable Blocks
help.modules.text: Modules are HTML building blocks that can be embedded in any template. Syntax: {{block:identifier}}
help.modules.available.title: Available Modules
help.modules.howto.title: How to use modules:
help.modules.howto.step1: 1. Click the 'Module' tab in the editor
help.modules.howto.step2: 2. Click a module → inserted at cursor position
help.modules.howto.step3: 3. Module appears as {{block:name}} in the HTML
help.modules.howto.step4: 4. On save/send, the block is automatically resolved

help.tutorial.s1.step1.title: Template Overview
help.tutorial.s1.step1.desc: Click the "Templates" tab at the top. Here you see all email templates — how many are active, draft, or archived. Use "+ New Template" at the top right to start a new email template.
help.tutorial.s1.step2.title: New Template — Start Options
help.tutorial.s1.step2.desc: After clicking "+ New Template", choose how to start: Blank Template (free design), Corporate Skeleton (with ready-made header and footer), or duplicate an existing template.
help.tutorial.s1.step3.title: Fill in Settings
help.tutorial.s1.step3.desc: Fill in the fields: display name, subject, technical name (identifier). The identifier is the internal name used in Python code — e.g. cv_generated_berater. It cannot be changed after the first save.
help.tutorial.s1.step4.title: Choose Sender Mode
help.tutorial.s1.step4.desc: Choose who appears as the sender. "User" = the email comes from the logged-in employee (e.g. angelo@abcona.de) with their signature. "Template" = fixed sender address. "Auto" = noreply, for automatic system mails.
help.tutorial.s1.step5.title: Write HTML and Insert Variables
help.tutorial.s1.step5.desc: In the middle area, write the email content. Under "Variables" in the sidebar you see all placeholders — click one to insert it. {name} is replaced with the recipient's real name on send.
help.tutorial.s1.step6.title: Live Preview and Test Email
help.tutorial.s1.step6.desc: On the right you see the live preview — how the email looks to the recipient. Switch between Outlook, Gmail, and TXT. In the sidebar under "Send Test Email" you can send a real test email to any address.
help.tutorial.s1.step7.title: Save — TXT Created Automatically
help.tutorial.s1.step7.desc: Click "Save" at the top right. Each save creates a new version with a timestamp. The TXT content (plain-text version) is automatically generated from the HTML — you don't need to maintain it manually.
help.tutorial.s2.step1.title: Open Version History
help.tutorial.s2.step1.desc: Click "Version History" in the blue bar. A panel opens with all saved versions. The green-highlighted version is the currently active one. Older versions can be restored.
help.tutorial.s2.step2.title: Change Note and Milestone
help.tutorial.s2.step2.desc: Before saving, enter a short note (e.g. "Logo updated"). Click "Mark" to mark the current version as a milestone — so you can find important versions quickly.
help.tutorial.s2.step3.title: Restore Version
help.tutorial.s2.step3.desc: Click an older version in the version history. After confirmation, that version is restored. The current version remains as a backup — you can switch back at any time.
help.tutorial.s3.step1.title: Open Translation Panel
help.tutorial.s3.step1.desc: Click "Translations" in the blue bar. A panel opens with all existing translations. DE is always the reference language — all other languages are translated from the German text.
help.tutorial.s3.step2.title: Activate Languages
help.tutorial.s3.step2.desc: Click "Languages" to open the language panel. Check the desired languages. Then click "Auto-Translate" in the bar — AI automatically translates all activated languages.
help.tutorial.s3.step3.title: Auto-Translate
help.tutorial.s3.step3.desc: Click "Auto-Translate" in the blue bar. AI automatically translates the entire email content. Important: variables like {name} or {cv_link} are never translated — they always remain as placeholders.
help.tutorial.s3.step4.title: Review and Edit Translation
help.tutorial.s3.step4.desc: Click the pencil icon (✏) next to a language to open the translation. You can edit and correct the text directly. After saving, your version is active and used on the next send.
help.tutorial.s4.step1.title: What are Modules?
help.tutorial.s4.step1.desc: Modules are ready-made building blocks you can embed in templates: Header (top area with abcona logo), Footer (bottom area with imprint), buttons and sections. Change a module once — it updates automatically in all templates that use it.
help.tutorial.s4.step2.title: Find Module in Sidebar
help.tutorial.s4.step2.desc: Scroll down in the left sidebar to "Modules". Modules are grouped by type: BUTTON, FOOTER, HEADER, SECTION. Click a module — it is inserted at the current cursor position in the HTML editor.
help.tutorial.s4.step3.title: Insert Module — Result
help.tutorial.s4.step3.desc: After clicking a module, a placeholder like {{block:abcona_header_blau}} appears in your HTML code. In the live preview on the right you immediately see how the module looks. On send, the placeholder is automatically replaced with the real content.
help.tutorial.s5.step1.title: When to Duplicate?
help.tutorial.s5.step1.desc: Duplicating makes sense when you need a similar template — e.g. a success mail and an error mail have almost the same structure. You save the entire base structure and only adjust the differing text.
help.tutorial.s5.step2.title: Duplicate Template
help.tutorial.s5.step2.desc: In the template overview, click the copy icon 📋 in the actions column. A dialog opens immediately where you give the copy a new name and a new technical name (identifier).
help.tutorial.s5.step3.title: Assign New Identifier
help.tutorial.s5.step3.desc: Give the copy a new display name and a new identifier. The identifier must be unique and cannot be identical to the original. All content (HTML, variables, modules, settings) is fully copied.
help.tutorial.s5.step4.title: Adjust Only the Differences
help.tutorial.s5.step4.desc: After duplicating, the studio of the new template opens immediately. Change only the text parts that should differ — e.g. subject, heading and error text. Layout, header and footer remain identical automatically.
